messages.author: 17e30776ec2a7fb1
messages.subject: install_github
parts:
After using install_github("whatever/pkg") suppose I later want to reinstall the same version of that package even if the github repo has since changed.

Is there some way to find out which version I installed and then later tell install_github to reinstall precisely that version?

messages.author: deea3c30b4c8409f
messages.subject: Re: install_github
parts:
You cannot add this info to the package version, unfortunately, because R package version strings are very restricted. (I suggested using semantic versioning and/or more flexible version strings on R-devel a couple of months ago, but it was turned down, not sure why.)

It seems that install_github adds info to the DESCRIPTION file, so if you do

> install_github("gaborcsardi/rappdirs@99034163bbbe108207f1bb838ea1630f5846a56b")

you can get what you need from

> packageDescription("rappdirs")
Package: rappdirs
[...]
GithubRepo: rappdirs
GithubUsername: gaborcsardi
GithubRef: 99034163bbbe108207f1bb838ea1630f5846a56b
GithubSHA1: 99034163bbbe108207f1bb838ea1630f5846a56b
[...]

Gabor

messages.author: b756a7daa2c2aa6d
messages.subject: Re: install_github
parts:
What do you mean by the "same version"? This is a bit tricky to
define in git, because the commits form a DACL, so it's not obvious
how, given a commit, to find the most up-to-date version of that code.
But maybe you're looking for something simpler?

Also, you may want to look into packrat, which is currently under very
active development, and also aims to solve this problem.

Hadley
